author: Epiphanius of Salamis
addressee: the Church, addressed as daughter Zion and the people assembled for the feast
occasion: A festal homily for Palm Sunday, celebrating Christ's entry into Jerusalem on a colt and contrasting the praise of the children with the hostility of the priests and Hebrews.
argument: The homily calls the whole Church to rejoice because Christ the King and Bridegroom comes again to Zion on a colt, bringing salvation, light, and truth while error, demons, and the curse are undone. It presents the Palm Sunday entry as the Lord's royal visitation, fulfilling prophecy and uniting heaven and earth in praise. The children's cry of 'Hosanna' is shown to be a true confession of Christ's divinity, inspired by Christ himself, while the priests and Hebrews reject him. The homily closes by affirming that the one seated on the colt is the eternal Creator and Lord of all, who remains in the Father's bosom and rules all creation.

outline.move: The preacher summons the Church and all creation to greet Christ the King and Bridegroom, who comes again to Zion on a colt, and to join the children in crying 'Hosanna'.
The Church is called to keep the feast spiritually, rejoicing that she has exchanged idolatry and pagan wisdom for the knowledge of the true God, and to see the nations gathered as her children.
The Gospel account of the entry is recalled, and prophets, angels, and all creation are summoned to join the festal acclamation of Christ.
The children's praise is contrasted with the priests' and Hebrews' rejection, and the children are presented as confessing that the one on the colt is the eternal Creator and Lord of all.

cast.name: Lazarus
cast.who: The man Christ raised from the dead the day before, mentioned as a sign of Christ's life-giving power.

cast.name: David

key_terms.sense: Palm branches carried in festal procession to honor Christ as victor over death
The Hebrew acclamation cried to Christ, interpreted as 'Save now'
The colt on which Christ rides into Jerusalem as on a throne
Christ as the Bridegroom of the Church and of incorruption
Daughter Zion, a prophetic title for the Church called to rejoice at the King's coming
The Church, the new people of God gathered from the nations
The synagogue, representing the old people that is left widowed while the Church rejoices
God has appeared or shone upon us, especially in Christ's coming
The Lord's coming or visitation, here his festal entry into Jerusalem
The feast being celebrated, the festal gathering of the Church
Knowledge of God, which has replaced idolatry in the Church

The Word, the eternal Son of God who became flesh and inspires the children's praise
The thrice-holy acclamation sung by the cherubim to the Lord
The bodiless powers, the angels, whose worship the Church imitates

_unresolved_facts.claim: Mary the sister of Lazarus, to whom Christ gave her brother back after four days; the Virgin Mary is mentioned separately as ἐκ Μαρίας κλάδῳ (branch from Mary).
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἀλλὰ τῇ Μαρίᾳ μὲν τετραήμερον νεκρόν· τῇ δὲ Ἐκκλησίᾳ τριήμερον ἑαυτὸν χαρίζεται ὁ Χριστός.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Mary the sister of Lazarus, to whom Christ gave her brother back after four days. The Virgin Mary is not mentioned separately; ἐκ Μαρίας κλάδῳ (branch from Mary) refers to Christ as the branch from Mary, not to Mary as a separate person in the cast.
David, source forms ['∆αβὶδ'] only. The form ∆αυὶδ does not appear in the source text.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The Hebrews/priests, quoted cry 'Let him be crucified' (Σταυρωθήτω, third person imperative, 'Let him be crucified')
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Hebrews/priests, quoted cry 'Σταυρωθήτω' (third person imperative, 'Let him be crucified'). The brief's parenthetical translation is correct but the Greek form is a third-person imperative, not a direct quotation from the priests as a voice; the text says the Hebrews 'cry out' (κράζουσιν) this, but it is presented as the narrator's report, not direct quoted speech marked as such.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The evangelist, introduced as 'the sacred herald evangelist' and quoted, sections ['u01-rem-mid']
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Τί γάρ φησιν ὁ ἱεροκῆρυξ εὐαγγελιστὴς τῆς ἑορτῆς, ἄκουσον· Ἐγένετο ὅτε ἤγγιζεν ὁ Κύριος εἰς Βηθφαγὴ...
_unresolved_facts.fix: The evangelist, introduced as 'the sacred herald evangelist of the feast' (ὁ ἱεροκῆρυξ εὐαγγελιστὴς τῆς ἑορτῆς) and quoted. The brief omits 'of the feast' (τῆς ἑορτῆς), which specifies this is the evangelist of this particular feast, not a generic title.
